content.title: AutoDesign: Meta-Harness Optimization for Long-Horizon Agentic Design
content.abstract: Transforming multimodal sources into condensed and structured media outputs can be fundamentally conceptualized as a long-horizon agentic process centered on a model-harness system. While an ideal harness system should align with human design priors and accumulate reusable experience through empirical exploration to drive recursive self-improvement, existing paradigms remain static and fall short of this capability. content.title: OmniScientist: An Omni-Modal Omni-Discipline AI Scientist
content.abstract: Recent advances in foundation models have enabled AI scientists to automate increasingly complete research workflows, from hypothesis generation and code execution to manuscript preparation. content.title: V-RAE: Rethinking Video Latent Spaces for Generation
content.abstract: Latent video generation relies on autoencoders to define a compact space in which generative models operate. Although video autoencoder architectures have evolved substantially, their latent spaces are still optimized primarily for pixel-level reconstruction and provide limited high-level semantic organization. content.title: Defensive Boosting for Online Probabilistic Forecasting
content.abstract: We study online probabilistic forecasting of binary outcomes chosen by an adaptive adversary. Given an online learning algorithm for a weak hypothesis class $H$, we would like to efficiently obtain two incomparable guarantees that existing online boosting techniques provide separately. content.title: Every PPT channel has finite entanglement-breaking index
content.abstract: We prove that every PPT linear map has finite entanglement-breaking index, thereby establishing the eventual entanglement-breaking property of PPT channels in full generality. content.abstract: LLM coding agents issue Bash commands through interfaces that may serialize, wrap, and reparse model output. content.title: Alaya-EVOKE: From Linear-Scaling Supervision to Endless World
content.abstract: Interactive world models must support persistent memory, responsive interaction, and long-horizon generation, yet these requirements place conflicting demands on the model. Maintaining history in the denoiser context or key-value cache incurs growing cost, forcing a trade-off between session length and retained memory, while low-latency interaction relies on few-step generation whose capabilities are bounded by its teacher. content.title: LittleLearner: Language Models Under Pedagogically Controlled Knowledge Exposure
content.abstract: Modern language models are trained on heterogeneous web-scale text corpora. Consequently, studying knowledge and skill acquisition is difficult, as prior exposure to related content is hard to characterize. To address this challenge, we introduce LITTLECURRICULUM, a curated 88B-token pretraining corpus tailored to U.S. elementary school material, explicitly excluding concepts, facts, and vocabulary taught above Grade 5. llm_enrichment.key_contribution: Introducing LITTLECURRICULUM, a curated pretraining corpus for language models to study knowledge and skill acquisition.

content.title: Skew Hives, Skew Skeps, Skew Schur Log-Concavity
content.abstract: Knutson and Tao's hives is a combinatorial model to compute Littlewood--Richardson coefficients. content.title: SAEVerbalizer: Generating Explanations for Sparse Autoencoder Features via Representation Verbalization
content.abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) are proposed to extract numerous features from large language model (LLM) representations, yet explaining these features still relies primarily on external observation. This reliance leads to superficial explanations inferred from observed model behavior and computational inefficiency from collecting such behavioral evidence at scale. llm_enrichment.key_contribution: Introducing SAEVerbalizer, a framework that generates explanations for sparse autoencoder features via representation verbalization.
